result.title: Unlearning at Speed: Rapid Activation Dampening for Efficient Machine Unlearning in Real-World Face Recognition
result.summary: Machine unlearning has become increasingly important in face recognition, where regulations like the GDPR empower users to request the removal of their personal data from deployed models. However, most existing unlearning methods are designed for closed-set classification with small-scale models and training data, and therefore do not generalize to real-world face recognition systems, which operate in an open-set setting with large-scale models and data. In this work, we propose Rapid Activation Dampening (RAD), a fast and targeted unlearning method tailored specifically for large-scale open-set face recognition. RAD approximates differences in average neuron activations between forget and retain identities, identifying and selectively suppressing neurons that are most associated with the targeted identity through a sensitivity-controlled dampening mechanism. We further propose the Forget Score (FS), which addresses the mismatch between existing unlearning metrics and open-set problems by providing a probabilistic interpretation of forgetting directly in the representation space. Experiments across several recent large-scale face recognition architectures and datasets show that RAD achieves strong forgetting while preserving overall model utility and substantially improving unlearning speed. These findings establish RAD as a scalable and practical approach to machine unlearning in face recognition systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Rapid Activation Dampening（RAD），通过估计遗忘身份与保留身份的平均神经元激活差异并选择性抑制相关神经元，实现大规模开集人脸识别的快速遗忘，并提出表示空间中的 Forget Score 评估指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作面向人脸识别的隐私合规遗忘，核心是身份级激活抑制与遗忘度量，不涉及多模态推理中的视觉细节保留、latent 状态生成或推理期证据使用，未见可供 LVR 借鉴的具体机制线索。
